chunks: The best adviser for himself is he who is the most obedient to his Lord, and the most deceiving for himself is he who is the most disobedient to his Lord. Deceived is he who deceived his own self. Enviable is he whose faith is safe. Fortunate is he who takes lesson from others, while unfortunate is he who fell victim to his desires and illusions.
ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of the truly fortunate and the unfortunate according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) defines true self-interest (nafs) as obedience to God, contrasting it with the self-deception of those who follow their whims (hawā). He further categorizes human states into the deceived, the enviable (those secure in faith), the fortunate (who learn from others' mistakes), and the wretched (those misled by illusion), reflecting the Shia emphasis on self-awareness and spiritual vigilance.

en.sayed-ali-raza: The best adviser for himself is he who is the most obedient to Allāh, and the most deceiving for himself is he who is the most disobedient to Allāh. Deceived is he who deceived his own self. Enviable is he whose Faith is safe. Fortunate is he who takes lesson from others, while unfortunate is he who fell victim to his desires.
